- If sentiment is consistently positive or neutral over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for the next 5–10 days.
- If sentiment turns negative or shows strong bearish signals, model often underestimates downside risk; increase forecast downward by 2–5% for the next 7–14 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% in 3–5 days), model frequently overcorrects and forecasts a prolonged upward trend; reduce forecast slope and add a downward bias of 1–2% per day for 5–10 days.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline after peak), model often fails to recognize it; apply a downward correction of 1–3% per day for 3–7 days.
- If model forecast is flat or rising slowly while sentiment is weak or negative, consider a downward bias of 1–2% per day for 5–10 days.
- For horizon > 14 days, model often underestimates volatility; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., -0.5 to -0.8), model tends to ignore the trend; apply a downward correction of 1–3% for 3–7 days after the spike.
